origins.section: 4.1 QMUX Sits on the Adaptor's Queues, Crossed
4.4 A Request on a Down Link Waits in the Queue
4.5 The Asynchronous Form Calls Back Once, With an Answer or With null
4.7.1 A Pool Takes the Name's Place

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-copied-queues: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-queues: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-queues: Section 4.1 says the copied QMUX "writes the purchase into `host-receive`, a queue only the adaptor should write to", that "the purchase never leaves the JVM", and that "every request returns `null` after its full timeout", which decides option a.
recorded.prompt:q-request-on-down-link: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-request-on-down-link: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-request-on-down-link: Section 4.4 says "`request` never checks the link. It puts the message on `host-send` with the timeout as its lifetime and waits. If the adaptor reconnects in time, the message goes out", and the first-ending output ends in "request returned 0210", which decides a (reconnecting 5 s after the call is well within 15 s).
recorded.prompt:q-slow-listener: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-listener: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-listener: Section 4.5 says "A response's callback runs on the adaptor's receiver thread, the one thread that reads the socket" and "A listener that does real work holds up the whole link", with the example where the host approved 000702 but the caller got null, which decides a by short inference.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-all-down: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-all-down: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-all-down: Section 4.7.1 says "With no member connected, the pool checks again every second until the timeout is spent and then returns `null` without handing the purchase to any member", which decides a.

recorded.prompt:q-copied-queues:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-queues:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-queues:b: Section 4.1 refutes this directly: the output shows "host received 0" and the text says "The purchase never leaves the JVM", so the host never gets it.
recorded.prompt:q-copied-queues:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-queues:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-queues:c: Section 4.1 refutes this directly: "Q2 logs nothing" and the request "returns `null` after its full timeout" (2000 ms in the output), so nothing fails at once.
recorded.prompt:q-copied-queues:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-copied-queues:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-copied-queues:d: Section 4.1 refutes this directly: "`isConnected()` is true because the adaptor's ready entry exists", and the request returns null rather than throwing.
recorded.prompt:q-request-on-down-link:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-request-on-down-link:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-request-on-down-link:b: Section 4.4 refutes this: `request` "waits" and returns `null` only when the message "expires in the queue unsent", and in the first ending it returned the 0210, so getting null at the moment of the call contradicts the page (partly by inference, since the page never mentions an adaptor "replay").
recorded.prompt:q-request-on-down-link:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-request-on-down-link:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-request-on-down-link:c: Section 4.4 refutes this directly: "`request` never checks the link", and only "`send` ... does check, and throws `ISOException` 'MUX is not connected'".
recorded.prompt:q-request-on-down-link:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-request-on-down-link:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-request-on-down-link:d: Section 4.4 refutes this directly: "If the adaptor reconnects in time, the message goes out", and the first ending shows "host received 1" after reconnecting, so the queue is not cleared.
recorded.prompt:q-slow-listener:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-listener:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-listener:b: By inference from section 4.5: the callback runs on "the one thread that reads the socket", so there is no free listener thread to wait for, and the 000702 example shows answers missing their timeout, not finishing in time.
recorded.prompt:q-slow-listener:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-listener:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-listener:c: Section 4.5 refutes this directly: the caller "get[s] its thread back at once", the output shows callbacks on `channel-receiver-host-receive` and `pool-2-thread-1` rather than `main`, and "Neither is yours".
recorded.prompt:q-slow-listener:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-listener:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-listener:d: By inference from section 4.5: responses run on "the adaptor's receiver thread, the one thread", and the 000702 example shows the second answer was not read while the first listener ran, so answers do not keep flowing.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-all-down:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-all-down:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-all-down:b: Section 4.7.1 refutes this directly: the pool returns null "without handing the purchase to any member".
recorded.prompt:q-pool-all-down:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-all-down:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-all-down:c: Section 4.7.1 refutes this directly: the blocking request returns null after the timeout ("000504: null after 3000 ms"), and only the listener form throws "No MUX available", and only after waiting.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-all-down:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-all-down:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-all-down:d: Section 4.7.1 refutes this directly: "`primary-secondary` uses the first member that is connected, so B takes over when A drops", and with none connected the pool returns null rather than throwing.
